t: You're looking at the Canada Memorial in Green Park. It commemorates members of the Canadian Forces killed during the First and Second World Wars. The Canadian sculptor Pierre Granche designed it, and it was erected in 1992 and unveiled by Queen Elizabeth the Second in 1994. It exists thanks to lobbying and fund raising, much of it in Canada, led by the former media tycoon Conrad Black. Granche was a French-Canadian sculptor who taught art history at the Université de Montréal for more than twenty years.
